items.shortLine: Meet Shira & walk through your plan
items.detailText: Get acquainted with Shira on your first day, walk through your onboarding plan together, and get clear on what's expected in the first weeks.

items.shortLine: Say hi to Lior, your buddy
items.detailText: Meet Lior, your Human Buddy — a low-stakes, always-available contact for the everyday questions that don't need to go through your manager.
Get physically oriented in the Tel Aviv office with Lior — where things are, how the space works, no manager required.
A self-paced session covering Veridian's vision, values, departments, and where we work — Tel Aviv HQ, London, and Austin. The first of six sessions on the company (1 of 6).
A short self-paced course covering the security basics everyone at Veridian needs to know.
A quick read on how we work together and what's expected of everyone at Veridian.
Email, calendar, and shared drive for day-to-day company communication — set up before you even start.
Slack access lands on Day 1 — where the AI Platform team and cross-functional partners communicate day to day.
Notion access is ready Day 1 — home for Veridian's engineering handbooks and the AI Platform team's own docs.
HiBob is ready Day 1 — your employee profile, time off requests, and the org chart.
Jira access arrives Day 2 — for tracking sprint work and tickets on the AI Platform team's board.
GitHub access is ready Day 3 — for opening PRs and code review on AI Platform's codebase.
Figma access lands Day 3 — handy for following along on product/design work that touches AI Platform's UI surfaces.
Get the full operating picture of the team from Shira in one sitting — mission, metrics, workflows, key interfaces, and where to find docs and reports.

items.shortLine: Meet the whole AI Platform team
items.detailText: Meet the 12 people you'll be working alongside day to day, in one sitting rather than waiting weeks for individual intros.
A self-paced look at what Veridian builds: Knowledge Hub, AI Assistant, AI Agents, and Governance. Session 2 of 6 on the company.
A self-paced session on Veridian's market and the kinds of customers it serves. Session 3 of 6 on the company.
A short course on data privacy fundamentals, required for everyone at Veridian.
A quick course on how Veridian reviews code — good to have under your belt before your first pull request.
A self-guided read through the handful of policies that matter most day to day — hybrid work, security, code review, deployments, expenses, and customer data.
A deeper course on writing secure code, tailored for engineers.
A self-paced session on Veridian's business model. Session 4 of 6 on the company.
A self-paced session on the key metrics Veridian tracks. Session 5 of 6 on the company.
Get set up on benefits and logistics, with a direct contact at HR from here on.
Stay aligned with Shira this week and flag anything that already feels off track.
A self-paced session on Veridian's strategic direction and near-term roadmap — the last of the six company sessions, now that you've got the fuller picture behind you.
Take a look at the Backend Engineer role profile to get a feel for how your role typically collaborates across the team.

items.shortLine: Say hello to Noa, your skip-level
items.detailText: Meet Noa Levi, Director of AI Engineering — the person who leads the broader group your team sits in.
A quick sync with Shira this week to catch anything before it piles up.
A session with Shira on where Engineering fits into Veridian and what it's aiming for this year.
This week's check-in doubles as your 30-day review — stepping back with Shira to see how the first month matched the plan and re-prioritize together.
Build a direct relationship with Tal Harari in People, beyond the initial HR intake session.
Your manager will pair you with a Professional Mentor soon to help with deeper technical guidance — we'll let you know as soon as that's set.
Keep the weekly rhythm going with Shira and raise anything that needs attention.
A short sync with Shira to stay in step and catch anything early.
Your weekly touchpoint with Shira — stay aligned and clear out any blockers.

internalGaps: DEMO ASSUMPTION (see prompts/process-expert.md and README.md): business-track LMS sessions 3-6 (market & customers, business model, key metrics, roadmap) have no real source data anywhere in this dataset - their descriptions are topical only. Must be validated against the real LMS before this assumption ships to production.

No explicit interface map exists for Veridian teams - nothing in this employee's context identifies which specific teams AI Platform interfaces with, so no Local/Global interface-contact meetings could be scheduled.

AI Platform has 12 people (6+), so per framework part D §11 only the mandatory group intro was scheduled - no data indicates which specific teammates are relevant to this employee's ongoing work, so no individual follow-ups were added.

Week 1 has 7 load units against the 6-unit cap - unavoidable given 3 Day-1-anchored people items, LMS session 1 (pinned to week 1), 2 trainings genuinely due by day 7, and the systems bundle. Flagged by the validator, not silently resolved - see plan gaps for the full breakdown.
The Engineering department overview (week 4) defaults to the direct manager as facilitator since no dedicated 'Trainer' role exists in this dataset.
This plan does not include applied 'doing' work tickets (out of scope by design for this pipeline).
